title: Billing Intake Routing & Prioritization Flow for Contracted Commitments and Marketplace Orders
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define an operational intake flow and an actionable prioritization rubric for non-bug billing requests coming from enterprise customers (commitments, invoicing edge-cases, cost allocation disputes, and marketplace order questions). This ticket consolidates decision criteria, routing responsibilities, SLA objectives, and example resolutions so that incoming requests are handled consistently and escalated to Finance, Sales Ops, or Engineering as appropriate. The output will be a lightweight operational runbook and a decision matrix embedded in the support triage UI.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single-page intake flow that support and Account Execs can follow to classify requests into: Commitments, Invoicing/Refunds, Cost Allocation, Marketplace Order Issues, Billing Data/Reporting. 2) A prioritization matrix with scoring factors (revenue at risk, legal/contractual exposure, engineering effort, compliance) and a documented SLA per class. 3) Routing table that maps classification to owners (Sales Ops, Finance, PM, Eng, Legal) and required artifacts. 4) Two pilot runs with real customer cases and documented outcomes. 5) Confluence runbook and triage checklist published and linked in Support handbook.
triage_flow: Step 1: Intake capture — support form captures request_type, customer_tier, contract_reference (if any), invoice_id, marketplace_order_id, and a one-line business impact description.
Step 2: Quick classification — use triage checklist to pick one category: Commitments, Invoicing/Refund, Cost Allocation/Chargeback, Marketplace Order, Billing Data & Reporting, Other.
Step 3: Immediate routing — auto-route high-revenue or legal-impact items to Sales Ops + Finance; medium-impact to PM + Finance; low-impact to Support queue with SLAs.
Step 4: Artifact collection — require attachments: signed commitment, invoice PDF, billing export snapshot, or marketplace order export URL before escalation to Engineering or Finance.
Step 5: Escalation decision — if code-level change or runtime billing bug suspected, tag ENG and include reproducible steps and sample payloads. If contractual ambiguity, tag Legal + Sales.

Step 6: Resolution path — map to standardized outcomes (refund, invoice correction, commitment re-pricing, allocation adjustment, policy clarification) with template communications for Support and Sales to use.
prioritization_matrix: Factors: Revenue at risk (0-5), Legal/Contract exposure (0-5), Time-sensitivity (0-5), Engineering effort (0-5), Customer strategic value (0-5)

Score calculation: Sum of factors. 0-6 = Low (P3, SLA 10 business days); 7-13 = Medium (P2, SLA 5 business days); 14-20 = High (P1, SLA 48 hours); >20 or any Legal exposure = P0 (Immediate exec review)
Tie-breakers: If scores are equal, use contract value then renewal date proximity as tie-breakers.
routing_table: Commitments (new or change requests) -> Sales Ops (owner) + PM review + Finance advisory; requires contract excerpt and expected revenue delta.
Invoicing / Refunds -> Finance (owner) + Support for customer comms; if invoice system bug -> Eng (owner) for root cause.
Cost Allocation / Chargebacks -> Finance (owner) + PM for allocation rule changes; requires billing export and allocation policy reference.
Marketplace Orders (3rd-party billing) -> Marketplace Ops (owner) + Finance + PM if product policy change required; requires marketplace order ID and vendor reconciliation file.
Billing Data & Reporting -> PM (owner) for spec + Eng for implementation; requires sample exports and desired schema.
decision_examples: Example A: Customer reports invoice double-charged and attaches invoice PDF. Classification: Invoicing/Refunds. Priority: Score=Revenue 3 + Legal 0 + Time 4 + Effort 1 + Strategic 2 = 10 -> Medium (P2). Route: Finance handles refund; Support sends templated acknowledgement within SLA.

Example B: Customer requests a 12-month commitment conversion to a different seat band and cites contract language. Classification: Commitments. Priority: Legal exposure 4 -> escalate to P0; route: Sales Ops + Legal + PM; require signed amendment before processing.

Example C: Marketplace order failed to settle with vendor causing missing credits. Classification: Marketplace Orders. Priority: High if renewal impacted; route: Marketplace Ops + Finance + PM; require vendor reconciliation file and customer order ID.
